title: Gabber bound for constructible sheaves on affine opens of an excellent strictly local scheme
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent strictly henselian local scheme of finite Krull dimension $d\geq0$, with $\ell$ invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every constructible sheaf $C$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the ordinary small etale site of $V$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], one has $$H^q(V,C)=0\qquad(q>d),$$ where $q$ is a nonnegative integer and $H^q$ is right-derived global-sections cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: Expose XV, Corollary 1.2.2, printed p. 219, applied to the affine open immersion f: V -> X (affine of finite type, X being Noetherian and affine), with the dimension function delta_X(t) = dim of the closure of {t}; then f_*delta_X = delta_X on V (XIV-2.5.2), so f_*delta_X(C) <= dim X = d and 1.2.2 gives H^q(V,C)=0 for q>d. Corollary 1.2.4 (printed p. 220) is the constant-coefficient case Z/n; the route is 1.2.2 directly, not the reduction of 1.2.3.
